knowledge:
- key_parameters: model=Formula specifying the probe-level model (e.g., PM ~ probes + samples) ;; constraint.type=Constraint applied to model factors (e.g., c(samples="contr.sum")) ;; variable.type=Specifies variable roles such as covariates (e.g., c(logliver="covariate")) ;; output.param=List to disable saving residuals or weights to save memory (e.g., list(residuals=FALSE, weights=FALSE)) ;; model.param=List to control fitting parameters like maximum iterations (e.g., list(max.its=0)) ;; background.method=Background correction method in threestep (e.g., "MASIM", "IdealMM") ;; normalize.method / normalize=Normalization method in threestep (e.g., "quantile") ;; summary.method=Summarization method in threestep (e.g., "tukey.biweight", "log.2nd.largest") ;; plot.method=Plotting style in MAplot (e.g., "smoothScatter", "add") ;; ref=Reference sample index or name for pairwise comparisons in MAplot ;; type=Type of residual image to plot (e.g., "resids", "pos.resids", "neg.resids", "sign.resids") or output type for RLE/NUSE (e.g., "stats")
- alternatives: rma from the affy package is a simpler alternative for standard preprocessing. fitPLM is preferred when detailed probe-level modeling, weights, residuals, or quality diagnostics (RLE, NUSE) are required. threestep is a highly flexible alternative to standard rma or mas5 workflows, allowing custom combinations of background correction, normalization, and summarization.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing Affymetrix microarray transcriptomics data and requiring advanced quality control diagnostics (such as Relative Log Expression (RLE), Normalized Unscaled Standard Error (NUSE), or spatial chip pseudo-images of weights and residuals) or when custom probe-level linear models are needed to account for covariates, probe types, or specific experimental designs.
- pitfalls: Fitting PLMs with full residuals and weights is highly memory-intensive; users should disable them via output.param=list(residuals=FALSE, weights=FALSE) if they are not needed. Setting max.its=0 disables robust estimation, which speeds up computation but removes robustness to outliers. Ensure older serialized AffyBatch objects are updated using updateObject() before fitting.

workflows.name: probe_level_modeling_and_qc
workflows.intent: Fit probe-level models to Affymetrix microarray data and perform comprehensive quality control diagnostics using spatial chip images, RLE, and NUSE.
input: Dilution (AffyBatch object representing raw microarray data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and update the AffyBatch object ;; 2. Fit a standard or customized probe-level model (PLM) ;; 3. Extract model coefficients and standard errors ;; 4. Generate spatial pseudo-images of weights and residuals ;; 5. Perform Relative Log Expression (RLE) and Normalized Unscaled Standard Error (NUSE) quality diagnostics
workflows.code:
library(affyPLM)
require(affydata)
data(Dilution)
Dilution = updateObject(Dilution)
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution)
coefs(Pset)[1:5,]
se(Pset)[1:5,]
verify.output.param()
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,output.param=list(residuals=FALSE,weights=FALSE))
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,model.param=list(max.its=0))
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,  MM ~ -1 + liver + scanner + probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs(Pset)[1,]
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
logliver <- log2(c(20,20,10,10))
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,model=PM~-1+probes+logliver+scanner, variable.type=c(logliver="covariate"),subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs(Pset)[1,]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,  PM ~ MM + samples + probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs(Pset)[1,]
coefs.const(Pset)[1,]
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,  PMMM ~ liver + probe.type + probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs(Pset)[1,]
coefs.const(Pset)[1,]
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,  PM ~ -1 + liver + liver:probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,   PMMM ~ -1 + liver + probe.type:probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution,   PMMM ~ -1 + liver + liver:probe.type:probes,subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs.probe(Pset)[1]
Pset <- fitPLM(Dilution, model = PM ~ probes + samples,constraint.type=c(samples="contr.sum"),subset = geneNames(Dilution)[1:100])
coefs.const(Pset)[1:2]
coefs(Pset)[1:2,]
image(Pset,which=2)
image(Pset,which=2,col=gray(0:25/25),add.legend=TRUE)
image(Pset,which=2,col=gray(25:0/25),add.legend=TRUE)
image(Pset,which=2, type="resids")
image(Pset,which=2, type="pos.resids")
image(Pset,which=2, type="neg.resids")
image(Pset,which=2, type="sign.resids")
image(Pset,which=2,type="resids",col=pseudoPalette(low="darkgreen",high="magenta",mid="lightgrey"),add.legend=TRUE)
image(Pset,which=2,type="pos.resids",col=pseudoPalette(low="yellow",high="darkblue"),add.legend=TRUE)
RLE(Pset,main="RLE for Dilution dataset")
RLE(Pset,type="stats")
NUSE(Pset,main="NUSE for Dilution dataset")
NUSE(Pset,type="stats")

workflows.name: flexible_threestep_preprocessing
workflows.intent: Preprocess AffyBatch microarray data using a flexible three-step framework (custom background correction, normalization, and summarization).
input: Dilution (AffyBatch object representing raw microarray data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and update the AffyBatch object ;; 2. Run the threestep function with default or customized background, normalization, and summarization methods
workflows.code:
library(affyPLM)
require(affydata)
data(Dilution)
Dilution = updateObject(Dilution)
eset <- threestep(Dilution)
eset <- threestep(Dilution, background.method = "MASIM", normalize.method="quantile",summary.method="tukey.biweight")
eset <- threestep(Dilution, background.method = "IdealMM", normalize="quantile",summary.method="log.2nd.largest")

workflows.name: intensity_dependent_ma_plots
workflows.intent: Generate advanced MA-plots to visualize intensity-dependent differences between microarray samples.
input: Dilution (AffyBatch object representing raw microarray data)
workflows.stages: 1. Preprocess the raw data to obtain an ExpressionSet ;; 2. Generate standard or smooth scatter MA-plots ;; 3. Customize MA-plots using reference samples, specific sample subsets, probe-state filters, or sample groups
workflows.code:
library(affyPLM)
require(affydata)
data(Dilution)
eset.Dilution <- rma(Dilution)
MAplot(eset.Dilution)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,plot.method="smoothScatter",nrpoints=256)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,ref=1,plot.method="smoothScatter",nrpoints=256)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,which=c(2,4),ref=1,plot.method="smoothScatter",nrpoints=256)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,which=c(1,2),ref=c(1,2),plot.method="smoothScatter",nrpoints=256)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,which=c("20A","20B"),ref=c("20A","20B"),plot.method="smoothScatter",nrpoints=256)
PA.calls <- mas5calls(Dilution)
Is.Present <- exprs(PA.calls) == "P"
Number.Present <- apply(Is.Present,1,sum)
MAplot(eset.Dilution[Number.Present ==4,],show.statistics=FALSE,which=1,pch=20,cex=0.4,ylim=c(-0.8,0.8),xlim=c(2,15),add.loess=FALSE)
MAplot(eset.Dilution[Number.Present ==0,],plot.method="add",col="red",which=1,pch=20,cex=0.4,show.statistics=FALSE,add.loess=FALSE)
MAplot(eset.Dilution[Number.Present ==3,],plot.method="add",show.statistics=FALSE,which=1,col="green",pch=20,cex=0.4,add.loess=FALSE)
MAplot(eset.Dilution[Number.Present ==2,],plot.method="add",show.statistics=FALSE,which=1,col="blue",pch=20,cex=0.4,add.loess=FALSE)
MAplot(eset.Dilution[Number.Present ==1,],plot.method="add",show.statistics=FALSE,which=1,col="orange",pch=20,cex=0.4,add.loess=FALSE)
MAplot(eset.Dilution,groups=c("Liver 20","Liver 20","Liver 10","Liver 10"),ref="Liver 10")
